annotations.title: Find the contacts that are probably one party

description: The active contacts of a company that are probably one party — two spellings of one customer, two imports of one supplier — strongest first, one row per contact to absorb. The rows that share a keep_id are one group (the contacts a chain of pairs joins); each names the contact to keep (the one of the group more ledger lines and documents name, then the older), the one to absorb, proposed_name (the simplest name the group carries — the fewest words carried by contacts outside the group, then the fewest words — a proposal for the kept contact, written only if the user wants it), a score from 0 to 1, the kinds of evidence (vat_number, registration_number, account: the same number or bank account, score 1; name: the words of the shorter name in the longer, each weighed by how few contacts carry it, so that a shared trade, place or legal form alone is never a pair; 0.950 for the same name, 0.900 otherwise, 0.600 when the shorter name agrees with several contacts) and the evidence in sentences. Two contacts with different VAT or registration numbers, a contact and its own parent, and inactive or merged contacts are never proposed. contact_types keeps the proposals among the contacts of those types — customer, supplier and both for the parties of the books — and every contact is read when it is absent. It writes nothing: show the user both contacts and call merge_contacts only on a pair they confirm, with the contact they choose to keep.

company_id.description: The company to work in. Ask list_companies if unsure.

contact_types.description: Propose only among the contacts of these types; every contact when absent.
